# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-33 (Extended v215)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to spring/summer Year 9. Primary Paris locations: Rue Plumet, Place de la Bastille, Prison Chargemagne, Rue de l'Homme Armé No. 6, Champ-de-Mars, Halles district, Rue du Pont-aux-Choux, Rue de Thorigny, Marché Saint-Jean, Rue des Billettes, Rue Saint-Denis, Rue de la Chanvrerie, Rue de la Petite-Truanderie, Rue Mondétour, Pointe Saint-Eustache, Rue du Cygne, Rue des Prêcheurs, Rue Blomet, Rue de Rivoli, Place Louis XV, Champs-Élysées, Esplanade, bridge of Invalides, Hôtel des Princes, Hôtel Meurice, Rue Saint-Honoré, Passage Delorme, Place du Palais-Royal, Rue de Béthisy, Rue des Bourdonnais, Rue de la Poterie, Rue du Contrat-Social, Marché-aux-Poirées, Rue de Babylone, Rue du Chaume, Rue des Vieilles-Haudriettes, Royal Printing Establishment, Luxembourg Garden, Rue de Pontoise, Rue Polonceau, Café Corinthe, Rue de l'Étoile, Rue Saint-Louis, Rue du Temple, Rue Vieille-du-Temple, Rue Notre-Dame de Nazareth, Rue Folie-Méricourt, Quai aux Fleurs, Rue du Petit-Musc, Rue du Normandie, Rue Pont-Aux-Biches, Rue des Marais, Faubourg Saint-Martin, Rue Notre Dame des-Victoires, Faubourg Montmartre, Rue Grange-Batelière, Rue Jacob, Rue de Tournon, Pont au Change, Pont-Neuf, Seine, Sainte-Avoye sewer, Rue Michel-le-Comte, sewer of the Louvre, Montmartre sewer, Rue du Cadran, belt sewer, Saint-Merry, Quay, Passy, Pont de Jéna, Bercy, Amelot sewer, Isle Louviers, Quartier Popincourt, Ménilmontant, Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire, Carrefour Boucherat, Corridor Saint-Louis, Saint-Gilles gut, Saint-Sebastian gallery, Arsenal, Faubourg Saint-Honoré, Quartier Saint-Georges, Quartier des Martyrs, gallery des Martyrs, Beautreillis sewer, Quai des Ormes, Grève, Place du Châtelet, Pont Notre-Dame, Quai de la Mégisserie, Boulevard, church of Saint-Paul, Rue du Parc-Royal, Madeleine, Rue Culture-Sainte-Catherine, Blancs-Manteaux, Place Royale, Tuileries, Rue Sainte-Croix-de-la-Bretonnerie, Rue de l'Écharpe, Rue Pavée, Rue des Trois-Pavillons. English locations: Kelmere, Elmhaven, Ostcombe, Dungate, Ravenmere, Staveford, Wilwick, Salcombe, Dunstead, Wilholt, Torton, Quenford, Pontoise, Stenenridge, Gulhaven, Barrière d'Enfer, Esplanade de l'Observatoire, Yarlby, Gagny, Lagny.

## English Subplot Summary

**Confirmed rumors**: Fire at Dunstead granary set deliberately. Stenenridge mill ledger rewritten after flood (confirmed by Wenelle Lindmere to Rovus Prydenridge, winter Year 8).

**Established facts**: Kassa Brackick and Volan Stenworth married at Staveford; Kassa went to Dungate. Taric Corrley quit Staveford for Dungate. Marald Corrford quit Dunstead for Salcombe; Fenelle followed. Ismira Stenson quit Dungate for Elmhaven (winter Year 6); Matho Stenson went to Elmhaven (winter Year 6). Elra Corrford settled in Elmhaven. Havie Prydenridge promised Gadrek Prydenridge to pay old debt to Stenworth family. Gadrek quit milling, took brewery work (autumn Year 7). Kassa Stenson's husband swore to rebuild fallen wall at Ostcombe. Fenelle found Elmhaven work (summer Year 7); Marald followed within month. Zavus Prydenridge apprenticed anew, became ferryman (summer Year 7). Islan Thornmere quit Ostcombe for Dungate (autumn Year 7); Vesmira Thornmere went to Dungate (autumn Year 7). Movie Prydenridge married Luena Stenenridge's only son at Ostcombe; couple lived there. Kassa Stenson kept promise to Taric Corrley: wall at Yarlby rebuilt by harvest. Havie and Isric Thornmere wed at Ostcombe with half parish present; lived there. Matho Stenson moved from Elmhaven to Staveford (winter Year 7); Fenelle followed Marald to Ravenmere within month. Elra Corrford rode out of Elmhaven; by next market day living in Gulhaven. Red Ismira went along to live in Staveford. Islan Thornmere died of old age at Dungate. Gadrek Prydenridge married Lura Haskick's eldest daughter in chapel at Ostcombe; couple lived there. Luvie Prydenridge and Semor wed at Ostcombe. Luena Stenenridge sent copper chalice by carrier to Yera Stenworth, who received it safely. Yera Haskick swore to Nerine Prydenridge to repair roof of chapel at Kelmere, shook on it. Havie Prydenridge never kept promise to Gadrek (pay old debt); matter abandoned. Luena Stenenridge left Wilwick, settled in Ostcombe. Rozek Stenenridge went along to live in Ostcombe. Luvie Prydenridge gave up weaving, took work as chandler (autumn Year 8). Ismira Stenson gave up being shepherd, took work as scribe (winter Year 8). Gadrek Prydenridge won copper chalice from Yera Stenworth at cards, fairly, kept it (winter Year 8). Tatho Brackick left Salcombe and settled in Wilholt. Yewyn Haskick followed him to Wilholt within the month. Ismira Stenson and Volan talked of weather, harvest, lame horse (Chapter 32).

**English Chapter 33 events (spring/summer Year 9)**: Pelde Stenson told Pelde Stenworth "You look tired"—Stenworth did not deny it. Dalis Stenworth told Davus "You look tired"—Davus did not deny it. Bell for vespers rang thinly across roofs; light went early. Davus argued with carter over price of sack of oats. Eldest daughter of Rorald Lindmere took Ilrald Prydenridge in marriage at Torton; couple lived there. Pelde mended torn sleeve by window, said little, fell asleep before fire caught. Frost silvered hedges overnight. Children chased hoop down lane, shrieking. Gulls quarreled over fish heads by steps. Road all ruts and puddles after thaw. Rain threatened since morning but held off. Rimor Corrford complained of aching back, as usual. Volan fell asleep in chair before fire caught. Kassa only shrugged when asked if it would rain. Ismira Stenson rode out of Staveford; by next market day she was living in Kelmere (late spring/early summer). Matho Stenson went along to live in Kelmere as well. Kassa Brackick complained of aching back, as usual. Price of salt discussed as scandalous. Volan complained of aching back, as usual. Rimor Corrford hummed tune from childhood while scrubbing step. Volan Stenworth laughed at story nobody else found funny. Somewhere a dog barked at nothing and then went quiet.

**Solemn promises**: Elra gave Matho promise to plant orchard on slope above Gulhaven. Pelia gave Fenelle promise to plant orchard on slope above Salcombe (summer Year 7). Movie swore to Nerine to plant orchard on slope above Wilholt, shook on it (autumn Year 7).

**Property transfers**: Kassa Brackick won bone compass from Volan Stenworth at cards, fairly, kept it. Kassa Brackick gave amber map to Volan Stenworth (summer Year 8). Kassa Brackick gave bone compass to Ismira (autumn Year 8).

## Marius and Cosette: Courtship, Revelation, Marriage, and Aftermath

**Spring Year 6 confessions**: Marius revealed—orphan, lawyer, father colonel and hero. Cosette revealed—raised at Petit-Picpus convent, mother dead, father M. Fauchelevent.

**Barricade and rescue (24 June)**: Éponine revealed leading Marius to barricade, gave letter from Cosette before dying. Marius joined barricade (6 June), witnessed M. Mabeuf's death, Bahorel killed. Shot broke collar bone. Vigorous hand seized him before consciousness vanished.

**Medical recovery (Chapters 27-30)**: Bullet deflected by pocket-book, serious laceration but not dangerous. Underground journey dislocated collar-bone seriously. Arms slashed with sabre cuts. Head covered with cuts. **7 September (four months after retrieval)**: Doctor declared Marius would recover. When Marius called grandfather "father" three times, Gillenormand agreed to bring Cosette to him.

**Cosette's arrival and revelation (Chapter 31)**: Learned she was not daughter of old man she called father; he was merely kinsman; another Fauchelevent was her real father. She was so full of joy cloud did not last long. She had Marius.

**Cosette's dowry (Chapter 31)**: Five hundred eighty thousand francs constituted legacy by dead person desiring to remain unknown.

**Gillenormand's gifts**: Called Cosette "exquisite darling," "masterpiece," warned half his possessions swallowed in annuity. Overwhelmed her with gallant compliments and presents: robes, lace, parures, ivory bon-bon boxes. Furnished chamber with elegant trifles.

**Wedding ceremony (1 February 1833, church of Saint-Paul)**: **Cosette wore white taffeta petticoat, Binche guipure robe, English point veil, fine pearl necklace, orange flower wreath.** Route: Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire. **Two maskers noticed wedding—Spaniard with enormous nose and huge black moustache; young girl masked with loup dressed as gaunt fishwife—held dialogue in low voice.** First coach held Cosette, Aunt Gillenormand, M. Gillenormand, Jean Valjean. Marius came in second coach. Both exchanged vows, signed registers, exchanged rings, knelt side by side under pall of white moire. **During dinner, Basque reported M. Fauchelevent suffering; injured hand paining him; begged excused; would come tomorrow. Had just taken departure. Jean Valjean had risen, gained antechamber unperceived during Cosette's command, left during celebration.**

**Jean Valjean's moral crisis (Chapter 31)**: In Cosette's empty bedroom: no sheets on bed. Pillow covered with ticking, without case or lace, laid on blankets. All little feminine objects Cosette attached to carried away; only heavy furniture and four walls remained. Toussaint's bed despoiled. One bed only made up—Jean Valjean's bed. **He opened inseparable portmanteau which never left him.** **Questioned: Should he force himself on this happiness? Should he treat it as belonging to him? Should he remain sort of father, half seen but respected? Should he present himself there as though he had right? Should he bring past to future?** **Remained twelve long hours of winter night, ice-cold, without raising head or uttering word. Motionless as corpse. All at once shuddered convulsively, mouth glued to Cosette's garments, kissed them; then it could be seen he was alive.**

## Javert's Death (Chapter 30)

**Moral transformation**: Javert's certainty crumbled. Duty divided within conscience. Valjean disconcerted him. All axioms crumbled. M. Madeleine reappeared behind Jean Valjean. Benevolent malefactor, merciful, gentle, helpful, clement. Javert constrained to admit monster existed. Supreme anguish was loss of certainty.

**Suicide (evening, Place du Châtelet)**: Took off hat, placed it on edge of quay. Tall black figure appeared erect on parapet, bent over towards Seine, drew self up, fell straight down into shadows; dull splash followed. Javert drowned.

## Marius's Crisis of Conscience and Jean Valjean's Decline (Chapters 32-33)

**Jean Valjean's revelation (morning after wedding—17 February)**: Jean Valjean appeared very pale, eyes hollow and sunken by sleeplessness. Black coat bore weary folds. **Proclaimed: "I am an ex-convict."** Marius stood with mouth wide open. Jean Valjean justified himself: conscience implacable; duty places one in hell where one feels God beside you. He had entered into engagements with himself; keeps them. Declared he revealed situation himself—nothing forced him. If police arrived, he would be exposed through his own act, not another's. Chose danger over security of false name.

**Marius's shock and philosophical reckoning**: Inward shudder of hideous enlightenment flashed through Marius. After Jean Valjean's departure, Marius pleaded with him not to tell Cosette: "She does not know what it is, it would terrify her. What, a convict!" Jean Valjean dropped into armchair, hid face in hands, seized with convulsion, tears inundating face. Marius later reflected: questioned whether he had failed in divination regarding Jean Valjean's nature. Admitted chimerical and visionary side of his nature. Recalled that during six or seven ecstatic weeks in Rue Plumet, he had not even spoken to Cosette of Gorbeau hovel drama, nor mentioned Thénardiers. Accounted for this: benumbed state, intoxication with Cosette, love absorbing everything, vague dull instinct impelling him to conceal that redoubtable adventure. Weighed everything: even had he discovered Jean Valjean was convict, it would not have changed him or Cosette. Would have adored her no less. Would not have refrained from marrying her. Therefore: nothing to regret. All was well.

**Jean Valjean's moral grandeur**: Jean Valjean had himself revealed situation. Nothing forced him. In avowal there was acceptance of peril. For condemned man, mask is shelter; false name is security. He had rejected false name. Galley-slave might have hidden forever in honest family; had withstood temptation. Through conscientious scruple. Mysterious rehabilitation begun; scruples controlled him long. Awakening of conscience is grandeur of soul.

**Marius's doubt about Javert and vengeance (RUMOR—UNCONFIRMED)**: Recalled Jean Valjean had been in barricade. Had not fought there. What came for? Spectre rose and replied: "Javert." Recalled funereal sight of Jean Valjean dragging pinioned Javert out of barricade. Heard behind corner of little Rue Mondétour frightful pistol shot. Obviously hatred between police spy and galley-slave. One in other's way. Jean Valjean had gone to barricade purpose of revenging himself. Arrived late. Probably knew Javert prisoner there. **Jean Valjean had killed Javert. At least, seemed evident.** [RUMOR—Marius has not verified this.]

**Marius's metaphysical rationalization**: Questioned what melancholy sport of Providence placed that child in contact with that man. Recalled biblical imagery: symbols of Genesis eternal; in human society there will always be two men—Abel (superior, according to good) and Cain (subterranean, according to evil). Conceptualized Jean Valjean as tender Cain, ruffian religiously absorbed in adoration of virgin, watching, rearing, guarding, dignifying, enveloping her. Pondered: What was this cesspool which had venerated innocence without leaving spot? In presence of double secret, Marius recoiled but then reasoned: God was visible in affair as was Jean Valjean. God has instruments; not responsible to men. Jean Valjean had labored over Cosette, made that soul—incontestable. But workman horrible; work admirable. God produces miracles as seems good. God constructs charming Cosette employing Jean Valjean. Dung-heap aids spring to create rose. Adored Cosette, possessed Cosette, Cosette splendidly pure. What enlightenment needed? Cosette light. Does light require enlightenment? He had everything. Jean Valjean's personal affairs did not concern him. Henceforth Marius to fulfill part of Providence to Cosette. Cosette, as she took flight winged and transfigured, left behind empty chrysalis: Jean Valjean.

**Marius's final conflicted position**: Forced to fall back upon: man was convict—being without place in social ladder, lower than lowest rung. Convict appeared hideous and repulsive. Still at point where had not distinguished between written by man and written by God, between law and right. Not examined right man takes to dispose of irrevocable and irreparable. Not shocked by vengeance. Found simple that certain breaches followed by eternal suffering, accepted social damnation as civilization process. Not wise to question sinister situations to last point, particularly when indissoluble side of life fatally intermingled. What terrible light from despairing explanations of Jean Valjean; whether hideous glare would dart forth as far as Cosette? Whether infernal glow lingered on brow of angel? Rightly or wrongly, Marius had been afraid. Already knew too much. Sought to dull senses rather than gain further light. Felt too good, too gentle, too weak. Weakness led to imprudent concession. Allowed himself touched; been in wrong. Ought have simply rejected Jean Valjean. But had promised, allowed drawn into promise; Jean Valjean held promise; must keep word even to convict. First duty to Cosette.

**Marius's investigation and moral uncertainty (Chapter 33)**: Encountered former employee of Laffitte establishment in legal case; acquired mysterious information about six hundred thousand francs without seeking it. Unable to probe out of respect for promised secret and consideration for Jean Valjean's perilous position. Believed he had grave duty to perform: restitution of money to someone sought with all possible discretion. In meanwhile, abstained from touching money.

**Chapter 33 domestic arrangements**: Nicolette (soldering of two elderly maids impossible with Toussaint) left. Grandfather well; Marius argued cases here and there; Aunt Gillenormand peacefully led life aside sufficient for her. Jean Valjean came every day. 

**Cosette's alienation from Jean Valjean (Chapter 33)**: Address as _thou_ disappeared, replaced by _you_, "Madame," "Monsieur Jean," rendering him another person. Care he had taken to detach her from him was succeeding. She became more gay, less tender. Still loved him sincerely, he felt it. One day chanced to say "father" to him. Flash of joy illuminated Jean Valjean's melancholy old countenance. He caught her up: "Say Jean."—"Ah! truly," she replied with burst of laughter, "Monsieur Jean."—"That is right," said he. Turned aside so she might not see him wipe eyes. **This was last time.** After that last flash of light, complete extinction ensued. No more familiarity, no more good-morning with kiss, never more that word so profoundly sweet: "My father!" He was at his own request and through his own complicity driven out of all his happinesses one after another; had this sorrow, that after losing Cosette wholly in one day, afterwards obliged to lose her again in detail.

**Jean Valjean's attempted solace (Chapter 33)**: When Jean Valjean wished to prolong visit and induce forgetfulness of hour, he sang praises of Marius; pronounced him handsome, noble, courageous, witty, eloquent, good. Cosette outdid him. Jean Valjean began again. Never weary. Marius—that word inexhaustible; those six letters contained volumes. In this manner, Jean Valjean contrived to remain long time.

**Cosette's confession about dowry (Chapter 33)**: Cosette chanced to say: "He said to me: 'Cosette, we have an income of thirty thousand livres. Twenty-seven that you own, and three that my grandfather gives me.' I replied: 'That makes thirty.' He went on: 'Would you have the courage to live on the three thousand?' I answered: 'Yes, on nothing. Provided that it was with you.' And then I asked: 'Why do you say that to me?' He replied: 'I wanted to know.'"

**Marius's crisis of doubt (Chapter 33)**: Jean Valjean found not word to answer. Cosette probably expected explanation. He listened in gloomy silence. Went back to Rue de l'Homme Armé; so deeply absorbed he mistook door and entered adjoining dwelling. Ascended nearly two stories before perceiving error and went down again. Mind swarming with conjectures. Evident that Marius had doubts as to origin of six hundred thousand francs, feared some source not pure. Perhaps discovered money came from Jean Valjean. Hesitated before suspicious fortune, disinclined to take it as own, preferring both he and Cosette remain poor rather than be rich with wealth not clean.

**Jean Valjean's withdrawal pattern (Chapter 33)**: Cosette paid no heed, passed evening and slept well as usual, thought of it only when woke. So happy! Speedily despatched Nicolette to M. Jean's house to inquire whether he were ill, why he had not come on previous evening. Nicolette brought reply: M. Jean not ill. Busy. Would come soon. As soon as able. Moreover, on point of taking little journey. Madame must remember it was his custom to take trips from time to time. Not to worry. Not to think of him. During last months of spring and first months of summer 1833, rare passers-by in Marais, petty shopkeepers, loungers on thresholds, noticed old man neatly clad in black, who emerged every day at same hour, towards nightfall, from Rue de l'Homme Armé, on side of Rue Sainte-Croix-de-la-Bretonnerie, passed in front of Blancs Manteaux, gained Rue Culture-Sainte-Catherine, and on arriving at Rue de l'Écharpe, turned left and entered Rue Saint-Louis. Soon he no longer came as far as Rue Saint-Louis. Got as far as Rue Pavée, shook head and turned back; then went no further than Rue des Trois-Pavillons; then did not overstep Blancs-Manteaux. One would have said pendulum no longer wound up, oscillations growing shorter before ceasing altogether. Every day emerged at same hour, undertook same trip, but no longer completed it, constantly shortened it. Whole countenance expressed single idea: What is use? Eye dim; no more radiance. Tears exhausted; no longer collected in corner of eye-lid; thoughtful eye dry. Old man's head still craned forward; chin moved at times; folds in gaunt neck painful to behold. Sometimes when weather bad, had umbrella under arm, but never opened it.

**Marius's estrangement strategy (Chapter 33)**: Marius, before marriage, put no questions to M. Fauchelevent; since that time, feared to put any to Jean Valjean. Regretted promise into which allowed himself drawn. Often said to himself done wrong making concession to despair. Confined himself to gradually estranging Jean Valjean from house and effacing him from Cosette's mind. Always placed himself between Cosette and Jean Valjean, sure in this way she would not perceive nor think of latter. More than effacement, it was eclipse.

**Cosette's magnetism (Chapter 33)**: Existed between Marius and Cosette all-powerful magnetism, which caused her to do, instinctively and almost mechanically, what Marius wished. Conscious of Marius' will in direction of "Monsieur Jean," she conformed to it. Husband had not been obliged to say anything; she yielded to vague but clear pressure of his tacit intentions, obeyed blindly. Her obedience consisted in not remembering what Marius forgot. Not obliged to make any effort. Without knowing why herself, without his having cause to accuse her, her soul had become so wholly her husband's that which was shrouded in gloom in Marius' mind became overcast in hers. However, in what concerns Jean Valjean, this forgetfulness and obliteration were merely superficial. Rather heedless than forgetful. At bottom, sincerely attached to man whom so long called her father; but loved her husband still more dearly. This had somewhat disturbed balance of her heart, which leaned to one side only.
